### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/master-detail.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**21** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/master-detail.ts`, `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectSchema (symbol, 41 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 33 pages)`, `sharingModel (literal, 43 pages)`
- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **145** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c866a6567b79b7d0a2faba44bf292bfca48e4b5e` — the merge of head `6582c1f0d8e30afbbb1386d731d524966075a46e` into base `d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c866a6567b79b7d0a2faba44bf292bfca48e4b5e && git checkout c866a6567b79b7d0a2faba44bf292bfca48e4b5e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4 6582c1f0d8e30afbbb1386d731d524966075a46e && git checkout -B drift-repro d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4 && git merge --no-ff 6582c1f0d8e30afbbb1386d731d524966075a46e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d4aaeaf0e2eb39ac574f1ba171a88535f9a678b4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ba6686ce6344a4e4d50b841dcb7c7550a94ed98a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23100 (body, triage `6133304643`, ruling `6134079470`, claim `6136101631`, dev report `6139196718`), PR #23179 (body, 20-file list, net diff against `main` at the head), the head's check-runs, `origin/main` at `e540e7ffb` for context, and the read-only HotCRM clone at `0f84c9c` for the three named producers. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Gate verdicts on this head, read at 2026-10-13T06:05Z:** 39 check-runs — 28 `success`, 5 `skipped` (the full-battery jobs that do not run on a PR head: `Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shard matrix, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`), 0 failed, and 6 still `in_progress` at this reading, reported as such and not assumed: `Test Core` shards 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, and `Type Check · workspace`. Of the required contexts, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` conclude `success`; `Test Core` (shard 5 `success`, five shards pending) and the workspace type check have not concluded. The verdict below is the contract verdict on the diff; the queue still waits for those six to conclude `success`, and a red among them re-opens this record.

### ① Derived judgments

Ruling B (`6134079470`): a `controlled_by_parent` object derives its master from exactly one required `master_detail`; the parse refuses the object with none or with two, naming the object and the rule; lint's `CBP_TIERS` collapses to one tier; the runtime's second tier (a non-required `master_detail`) and third tier (a required `lookup`) retire under ADR-0049 with an ADR-0087 disposition and a BREAKING changeset naming HotCRM's three objects. Every accept-set and public-surface change the diff implies, judged against that:

1. **Parse refusal — RIGHT.** `refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster` sits in `ObjectSchemaBase`'s superRefine beside the existing checks, so it reaches raw `.parse()`/`.safeParse()`, `ObjectSchema.create()`, `defineStack`, `os validate` and the save door, which is what the ruling's "the parse (`ObjectSchema`) refuses" means. Zero required masters are reported at `sharingModel` naming each field that relied on a retired tier; two or more at `fields`; both messages name the object and ADR-0055 §1. It judges the PARSED field map, where `required` defaults to `false`, so a plain-literal `master_detail` with `required` omitted is refused while `create()`'s existing #9138 force still passes it — the builder's convenience is not the rule, and the ruling said the parse. Other sharing models are left alone (pinned). `fields` is a record on `ObjectSchema`, so the array-form early return in the helper is unreachable there and harmless. The ADR-0055 anchor added for `object.zod.ts` states this invariant. Right.
2. **Lint's new verdicts — RIGHT.** `CBP_TIERS` is gone; `cbpMasterCandidates` is the one predicate (`master_detail`, `required === true`, with a `reference`). `security-controlled-by-parent-no-relation` now fires on the non-required `master_detail` and the required `lookup`; `security-controlled-by-parent-ambiguous-relation` fires on two or more required `master_detail` fields with the verdict "no master is derived" and names no winner, which is the runtime's new answer, so the module header's "one exception" paragraph is correctly retired. `required` is read as `=== true` (was truthy), matching the runtime's new read. `security-master-detail-ungranted` stops treating a lookup-bound `controlled_by_parent` object as a child: consistent, since the runtime derives nothing from it any more and the no-relation error speaks. The new `it.each` holds the lint equal to the parse on the five ruled shapes and asserts the accepted shape parses whole. Right.
3. **Runtime resolver — RIGHT, with one choice beyond the ruling's wording, judged right.** `resolveCbpRelation` resolves exactly one required `master_detail` naming a reference and otherwise `null`, which both legs already treat as fail-closed (reads `RLS_DENY_FILTER`, writes `MasterDetailRelationMissingError`, 422 `INVALID_METADATA`). The ruling named tiers two and three for the runtime; the diff also refuses TWO required `master_detail` fields instead of picking the first by field order. That follows ADR-0055 §1's "exactly one … fail closed" and the ruling's own sentence "derives its master from exactly one required `master_detail`", it removes the #14747 order-dependence the lint already called an error, and it is what makes the three seams agree; recording a first-by-order pick would have kept the inference ruling B refused in option A. Right. The reference-spelling tolerance (`reference_to`/`referenceTo`, a separate ruling) is untouched: right. `reportCbpMasterUnresolved` warns once per object per cache generation (its only call site is the `cbpRelCache` miss body), is gated on `masterGovernsRowWrites(schema)` so a non-`controlled_by_parent` caller never reports, and names the retired shape the object relied on: right, a denial that is an empty result must not be silent. Reading `required` as `=== true` means a raw-registered object with a non-boolean truthy `required` on its master now fails closed; the spec's type is boolean and the lint reads the same, so accepted.
4. **Error-message text — RIGHT.** `MasterDetailRelationMissingError` now says "not exactly one required master_detail field" with the remedy "Declare one master_detail field with required: true", and the explain-engine condition string follows. The old sentence ("no master_detail relation") was false for the tier-two and two-master cases this PR routes to the same 422. No other consumer of the old text exists on `main` outside the three changed files. Same code, same status, no new `ERROR_CODE_LEDGER` row, so the claim's `Clause-②: no` stands. Right.
5. **ADR-0087 disposition — RIGHT, one residual named.** `registered cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired`: a new step-18 D3 semantic entry (`surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`, filename derived from the id, registry row generated, no index to edit) and no D2 conversion. For the required-`lookup` tier that is correct: a lookup turned `master_detail` changes what deleting the master does to every row, and whether the object should instead leave `controlled_by_parent` is the author's decision, so no lossless mapping exists and ADR-0087 D2 excludes it. For the non-required-`master_detail` tier the dev's "neither shape maps losslessly" is weaker: an OMITTED `required` on the one `master_detail` of a `controlled_by_parent` object maps to `required: true` exactly as the builder's own #9138 force already maps it, and ADR-0087 D2 would ordinarily ship that as a stored-row conversion so a row at rest keeps serving. The chosen refusal is the conservative direction and is within the ruling (which orders the raw-parse refusal and names no conversion), the row still registers under `[metadata_spec_invalid]` and is reported once rather than dropped (ADR-0087's stored-metadata addendum, #3903, "reads diagnose, never drop", is honoured), and major 18 is unreleased. Accepted; the residual is in ③ with a carrier. Stored tier-two and tier-three rows: diagnosed at registration, denied by the runtime, prescribed by the entry. Right.
6. **The two amended sibling step-18 entries — RIGHT.** `cbp-master-detail-required-forced` and `cbp-master-detail-required-lint-error` are prescriptions `os migrate meta` prints to a consumer, not decision records; their "raw parse stays tolerant" and "the runtime keeps resolving the master for metadata at rest" sentences became false the moment this PR lands, and a step that contradicts itself is a worse record than one amended in place. Ids and surfaces unchanged, the amendments point at the new entry by id. Right.
7. **ADR-0055 itself — untouched, RIGHT.** The PR implements §1 as written; no amendment is owed, no `docs/adr/**` path is in the diff (not Tier H), and both load-bearing spots gained an ADR-0055 anchor (`check:adr-anchors` green).
8. **Docs — two pages right, one page missed.** `error-catalog.mdx` and `error-handling.mdx` drop the non-required `master_detail` and required `lookup` rows from the 422 `MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD` matrix and say why: right. MISSED: `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` (the security publish linter bullet) still describes the no-relation rule's trigger as "no required `master_detail`, no `master_detail` at all, and no required `lookup`", which is the three-tier emptiness; after this PR a required `lookup` alone IS reported, so the sentence now understates the rule in exactly the direction the ruling closed. One sentence, not in the diff. Carrier in ③.
9. **Fixture triage — right, one fixture missed.** Every `controlled_by_parent` fixture the dev's table names is re-judged correctly; the in-tree authored objects (`crm_opportunity_line_item`, `showcase_expense_line`, `showcase_invoice_line`) and the dogfood fixtures declare `required: true` and stay legal; the plugin-security suites that register schemas raw all declare `required: true` on their master. Missed: `packages/objectql/src/engine-unreadable-master-detail-header.test.ts` builds `uh_cbp_line` as `controlled_by_parent` over `invoiceField`, a `master_detail` with no `required`. objectql boots no security plugin and its registry's spec check is diagnostic-only, so the suite stays green, but the fixture is no longer a §1-legal shape. One-line respell; carrier in ③.
10. **Public surface.** No export, signature, JSON-schema key or error code is added or removed (`check:api-surface` unchanged, `check:generated` green). The one new runtime behaviour an operator sees is the warn line; the one new author-facing text is the parse issue. Nothing is advertised that the runtime does not deliver.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/23100-cbp-one-required-master.md`: `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/plugin-security` at `minor`, title with the breaking bang, body headed BREAKING, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired`), and the `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` line. That is the launch-window convention (a breaking change ships as `minor` while the fixed group is in lockstep; `check:changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` green) and it matches what the diff publishes: a narrowed `ObjectSchema` accept-set, new lint error verdicts, a narrowed runtime resolver. **Matches.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is right: no new key on any published payload; a narrowing is BREAKING, and the changeset says so. The PR body carries the same line.
- FROM → TO names HotCRM's three objects, and the FROM column is verified on the clone at `0f84c9c`: `crm_campaign_member.crm_campaign` and `crm_event_attendee.crm_event` are `Field.lookup(…, { required: true })` with no `deleteBehavior` (so the engine's required-lookup escalation refuses the parent delete today, which both objects' own comments say is intended); `crm_article_feedback.crm_knowledge_article` is `Field.lookup(…, { required: true, deleteBehavior: 'cascade' })`. The other five `controlled_by_parent` objects each declare one required `Field.masterDetail`. The TO prescribes `deleteBehavior: 'restrict'` for the first two to keep that behaviour; that diverges from the ruling's hotcrm sentence "delete semantics become cascade", and the divergence is routed to the hotcrm card's filer (③). The migration is one line and shippable in CHANGELOG. Right.
- No changeset owed for `@objectstack/verify` (test file only) or `@objectstack/objectql` (header comment only); `Check Changeset` / `check:empty-changeset` green.

### ③ Boundary flags

Every dev deviation and every out-of-scope finding in `6139196718`, answered or escalated. `open_questions` was empty.

Deviations:

1. *File-surface breaches in plugin-security outside `resolveCbpRelation`* (`reportCbpMasterUnresolved`, the `errors.ts` message, the explain-engine condition, the `computeControlledByParentFilter` docblock, one SUPERSEDED bullet in the write-gate freeze note) — **answered, accepted**: each is text or a reporter the rule change made false or necessary; none is in the regions PR #23114 or #22900 edited, and both landed and are merged into this head.
2. *Further breaches* (`rule-explanations.ts`, the objectql `master-detail.ts` header, two docs pages, the two sibling step-18 entries, two ADR-0055 anchors, the verify test) — **answered, accepted** for the same reason; the docs sweep is short by one page (① 8) and the fixture sweep by one file (① 9).
3. *The runtime refuses two required `master_detail` fields instead of picking the first* — **answered, accepted** as ① 3: ADR-0055 §1 and the ruling's "exactly one" cover it; it is a narrowing the lint already graded an error, not a widening.
4. *PR opened after the readings were in* and 5. *lock-queue time* — process notes, no contract effect.

Out-of-scope findings:

- *verify `masterLinkOf` zero-master tail and the two-master branch counting non-required masters; `notDerivable` unreachable for a §1-legal detail* — **answered, accepted as acceptance notes**: report-line text in a branch no parse-legal object reaches; not a defect, a contract violation or an authoring trap, so a note is the right carrier.
- *Stale freeze note in `assertControlledByParentWrite`* — **accepted**: pre-existing, only its first-shape bullet is touched here.
- *HotCRM `restrict` vs the ruling's "cascade"* — **confirmed on the clone and escalated with the carrier the dev named**: whoever files the ruling's hotcrm card (the hotcrm seat at hotcrm#1353, or triage) carries the choice; the fork clause keeps letter B either way.
- *`ObjectExtensionSchema` is not judged by the one-master rule* — **escalated**: an extension that adds a second required `master_detail` to a `controlled_by_parent` base is refused at no parse and goes dark at runtime (fail-closed, reported once). The ruling named `ObjectSchema`, so this PR is not short; but "code read only, not measured" on a shape an author can write is a metadata-authoring trap candidate, which Prime Directive #10 files rather than notes. Carrier: the dispatching seat files it as a finding (measure whether the merged object is re-parsed with a diagnostic and whether the warn fires; decide whether the extension seam owes the same refinement).

Items this review adds (none blocks the verdict; each has a carrier):

- **`content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx`** — the three-tier sentence in the security-linter bullet (① 8). Carrier: the dev, as a docs-only follow-up on this card, or on this PR if it re-spins for any other reason.
- **`packages/objectql/src/engine-unreadable-master-detail-header.test.ts`** — `invoiceField` gains `required: true` so `uh_cbp_line` is a §1-legal fixture (① 9). Same carrier.
- **`STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment** — the entries README says a step-18 retirement adds its fragment to `registry.ts.template`; none was added. 116 fragments stand against 357 step-18 entries and the two sibling cbp entries carry none either, and no gate pins parity, so this is a convention gap shared with its siblings, not a contract breach. Same carrier.
- **D2 for the omitted-`required` half** (① 5) — a stored `controlled_by_parent` row whose one `master_detail` omits `required` goes dark on the 17 → 18 upgrade with a diagnostic and one warn where a lossless conversion (the builder's own force) would keep it serving. Carrier: the owning seat decides before 18 ships whether to add that one conversion or record in the entry why not; the ruling itself does not require it.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-23100-cbp-one-master`
Reviewed-by: `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6582c1f0d8e30afbbb1386d731d524966075a46e`
Local-runs: none

Review after patch round 1. Inputs read: card #23100 (body; triage `6133304643`, ruling `6134079470`, claim `6136101631`, dev reports `6139196718` and `6141838120`, ACCEPT `6139237069`), PR #23179 (body, 25-file list, both comments including the round-0 record `6139386784`, and the net diff against `main` at this head's merge base `20949e7a7`), the head's check-runs, `origin/main` at `150da61aa` for context, objectui `origin/main` at `cea429b98` and the pinned `1fb1ced36` for the Studio writer, and the read-only HotCRM clone at `0f84c9c`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Gate verdicts on this head, read at 2026-10-13T08:56Z:** 48 check-runs — 41 `success`, 7 `skipped`, 0 failed, 0 in progress. The skipped seven are the full-battery jobs a PR head does not run (`Console Pin Gate`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the dogfood shard matrix, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`) plus `Check PR Size` and `Auto Label` on a second workflow run whose trigger does not fire them. All five required contexts conclude `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (and each of its six shards), `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on both of its runs; the second (started 08:49Z) was still `in_progress` at this review's first reading and had concluded by the time this record was written.

**Round scope, measured.** The PR-side edits since `ba6686ce6` are exactly the eight files the dev lists. Three more files differ between the two heads (`packages/lint/src/rule-explanations.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts`), but each one's PR-side net diff — against `02bec6ca8` for the old head and `20949e7a7` for this one — is byte-identical: `main` moved underneath them in merge `e09bd7673`, nothing on the PR side did. Round 0's judgments (record `6139386784` ① 1–10) were re-read on this head and stand; this record repeats them only where round 1 touched them.

### ① Derived judgments

**The earlier record's four carried items, each answered.**

1. **`content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx` — DONE, right.** The security-linter bullet now reads "without exactly one required `master_detail` to derive access from (ADR-0055 §1: `security-controlled-by-parent-no-relation` when it declares none — a `master_detail` without `required: true` and a required `lookup` derive nothing — and `security-controlled-by-parent-ambiguous-relation` when it declares two or more; either way the runtime denies every read and refuses every write)". Every clause is what `cbpMasterCandidates` and `resolveCbpRelation` do on this head; the three-tier sentence is gone.
2. **`packages/objectql/src/engine-unreadable-master-detail-header.test.ts` — DONE, right.** `CBP_LINE_OBJECT` now spreads `REQ_LINE_OBJECT.fields` and overrides `invoice` with `{ ...invoiceField, required: true }`, on that object alone; the plain, `requiredWhen` and `readonlyWhen` fixtures keep the shared `invoiceField` unchanged. `uh_cbp_line` is a §1-legal shape, and the docblock says why.
3. **`STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment — DONE, right.** Id `cbp-master-relation-tiers-retired`, `order: 95` (the template's max on `main` is 94), inserted in id order ahead of `chart-config-aria-retired` — the shape `step18-rationale-merge.test.ts` pins (sorted by id, explicit order). The text states the one-master rule, the two retired tiers, the fail-closed runtime answer, the one converted shape and its producer, the retirement from the load path, and the three shapes not converted. Accurate to the code. (The two sibling cbp entries still carry no fragment; that is their pre-existing gap, not this PR's.)
4. **D2 for the omitted-`required` half — DONE.** Judged in full in 5–9.

**The new D2 conversion `cbp-master-detail-required-defaulted`, judged as a contract change.**

5. **Lossless — RIGHT.** The transform writes `required: true` onto the one `master_detail` of a `controlled_by_parent` object when the key is absent. That is byte-for-byte what `ObjectSchema.create()` has emitted for the same source since #9138: `forceCbpMasterDetailRequired` on this head forces an omitted `required` to `true`, throws on an explicit `false`, and leaves `true` alone — so a stored Studio row and a builder-authored object with the same declaration now serve the same object. The master it resolves under 18 (the one required `master_detail`) is the master tier 2 resolved under 17 (any `master_detail`; with one there was no pick). Under 18 the un-converted shape does not parse at all (`refuseControlledByParentWithoutOneMaster` refuses it at `sharingModel`), so the replay is a rescue of a row that would otherwise register under `[metadata_spec_invalid]` and be denied every read — not a reinterpretation of a shape that still parses, which is the artifact door's `DEFAULT_FLIPS_NOT_REPLAYED_HERE` criterion; no row is owed there. No DDL path reads `field.required` (grep over the drivers' and objectql's schema paths on `main`: none). The one write whose answer changes is the subject of ③ item A: a by-id PATCH that explicitly nulls the master FK — accepted on a non-required master because the write gate reads the STORED row's FK on update and never the incoming value, refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` by the record-validator's ADR-0113 check once `required` is `true`. Before, that write minted a detail row no `controlled_by_parent` read filter can ever match (the gate's own freeze note names it as the defect); the conversion closes that route for data at rest exactly as the builder's force closes it for authored objects. That is the contract's intent, not a capability lost, so lossless stands.
6. **Scope — exactly the one shape, RIGHT.** Read line by line: `obj.sharingModel !== 'controlled_by_parent'` returns; `fields` must be a dict; `masters` are the fields with `type === 'master_detail'` irrespective of `required`, and `masters.length !== 1` returns — so zero masters and two or more are untouched; `'required' in def` returns — so an explicit `false` (and an explicit `true`) is untouched; a `lookup` is never a candidate, so the required-`lookup` tier is untouched, while a required `lookup` BESIDE the one `master_detail` does not block the conversion — right, because the parse accepts a required master beside lookups and tier 2 outranked tier 3, so the same master resolves.
